title: Gasoline demand across fourteen regions
intro:
Illustrative data, made up for this book. An analyst has, for fourteen regions in one year, the average price of gasoline ($ per gallon) and the gasoline bought per person (gallons per year). Fit the log–log model ln(gallons) = b₀ + b₁ ln(price).

Give the price elasticity b₁, the 95 % interval for it, and R², each to three decimals.

In the Workbench: **Copy the data**, Ctrl+B, **+ Data table**, Ctrl+V. Choose **Simple linear regression**, set **x column** to *Price ($/gal)*, **y column** to *Gallons per person*, and both **Transform x** and **Transform y** to *Log*. Ctrl+L brings you back.
hints: Take the natural logarithm of both columns first: x = ln(price), y = ln(gallons). Then it is an ordinary least-squares line (item 11.2).
The slope of a log–log line is the elasticity: the percentage change in quantity for a 1 % change in price. Demand elasticities are negative.
In R: fit <- lm(log(gallons) ~ log(price)); coef(fit); confint(fit); summary(fit)$r.squared.
